title: Token Jumping in Planar Graphs has Linear Sized Kernels

predicted_errors.error_location: Definition of the projection classes and construction of G' following Claim 4
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The classes C_Y are defined over all of V(G), not over V(G) \ X. Consequently, vertices of X=I_s∪I_t may themselves lie in C_2 and even in N^{Int}(Y) for an X-pair Y. The reduction deletes vertices from \(\bigcup_{Y\in\mathcal P_{Big}}N^{Int}(Y)\), without excluding X. It can therefore delete a source or target token vertex, in which case ISR-TJ(G',I_s,I_t) is not even a valid instance. Standard projection-class arguments must define the classes on V(G)\X, or explicitly protect X.

predicted_errors.error_location: Claim 7, P^2 case: “Recall ... N^{Int}(Y_i) contains non-adjacent vertices that lie in J_m”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: This does not follow from the definition of J_m. J_m is only an arbitrary independent set of size k in the union of all big interior classes. Although each Y_i in P_Big has two nonadjacent interior vertices, J_m need not contain any vertex of a particular Y_i, much less two specified nonadjacent vertices from every Y_i. Indeed, there can be more such classes than k, so J_m cannot contain two vertices from each of them. The vertices z_i',z_i'' used in the subsequent induction are therefore unjustified and may not exist.

predicted_errors.error_location: Claim 7, P^2 case, induction beginning “For the base case, we move the token on y_1'' to z_1'”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proposed jump is generally illegal. Every z_1' in C_{Y_1}, where Y_1={y_1',y_1''}, is adjacent to both y_1' and y_1''. The construction starts from I_s, so both y_1' and y_1'' initially carry tokens. The proof invokes the fact that a witness sequence σ previously moved a token off y_1', but it does not reproduce that move in its newly constructed reconfiguration. Thus y_1' remains occupied when it attempts to jump y_1'' to z_1', violating independence. The asserted induction invariant is not established either, so the later jumps are likewise unsupported.

predicted_errors.error_location: Paragraph immediately before Claim 7: “Since G[J_s \cup J_t \cup J_m] is a linear forest, by Claim 4 ... YES”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The claim that this induced graph is a linear forest is neither proved nor implied by Claim 3. Claim 3 only excludes edges between interior vertices belonging to distinct X-pairs. J_s and J_t explicitly include leftmost/rightmost boundary vertices of classes, for which Claim 3 gives no such nonadjacency guarantee; edges involving these retained boundary vertices can create inter-class edges and cycles. Moreover, Claim 4 is a size bound conditional on an independent-set test, not the reconfiguration statement needed here; Claim 5 is the stated linear-forest reconfiguration result. This unsupported assertion is essential to the claimed YES conclusion and hence to equivalence.

The text calls itself the “full text” but contains no bibliography or reference list identifying any numbered citation. Consequently, key attribution-dependent claims—including that Ito, Kamiński, and Ono [4] proved fixed-parameter tractability, that [1] asked the linear-kernel question, and that [3,5] provide the stated linear-time embedding algorithm—cannot be checked. The missing references must be supplied, with complete and correct bibliographic details.
